paper.title_en: Suppressing noise in quantum random access codes via non-Hermitian operations
paper.abstract_en: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) constitute a fundamental framework for demonstrating the advantages of quantum resources and protocols, with wide-ranging applications in quantum information processing. In this work, we investigate the influence of parity-time (<math><mi mathvariant="script">PT</mi></math>) symmetric non-Hermitian operations on noisy QRACs using an analytically tractable two-level model. Focusing on the <math><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> QRAC, we show that non-Hermitian operations can enhance the dimension witness and restore quantum advantage in the presence of amplitude-damping, phase-damping, and phase-flip noise channels with appropriate parameters. We further analyze the limiting behavior of the model. Our results provide a proof-of-principle demonstration that suitably chosen non-Hermitian operations can improve the noise robustness of the <math><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> QRACs.
